## One week to go 📅 {.smaller}

Next week: your **15 minutes** with me 💬

Today:

- how the exam will look 🎓
- last checks on your project ✅
- work time, I am here 🛟

::: notes
0–5 min. Calm, practical tone. Exam anxiety peaks now.
:::

## How the 15 minutes will go 💬 {.smaller}

| Minutes | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | You share your screen and **run** your tool ⚙️ |
| 3–8 | You walk me through the code 🚶 |
| 8–13 | I ask questions about your choices 🤔 |
| 13–15 | What was hardest, what would you change 💭 |

. . .

No memorising. No trick questions. Your code is open in front of you 📖

::: notes
5–15 min. Being explicit about the structure removes most of the fear.
:::

## Questions I will probably ask 🤔 {.smaller}

- Walk me through what happens when I run this command ⚙️
- Why a dictionary here and a list there?
- What happens if the input file is empty? 🛡️
- Which part took you longest? 😅
- If you had another week, what would you add?
- Where did you get stuck, and how did you get unstuck? 🔍

. . .

"I don't know, but here is how I would find out" is a **good** answer 💛

::: notes
15–25 min. The last line matters — reward honesty over performance.
:::

## Final checklist ✅ {.smaller}

- [ ] Runs from the terminal with an argument ⚙️
- [ ] At least 3 functions with clear names 🧩
- [ ] Reads a real file 📄
- [ ] Prints or saves output 💾
- [ ] Friendly message when input is missing 🛡️
- [ ] README with an example command 📖
- [ ] Commits spread over several days 📈
- [ ] **You can explain every line** 🗣️

::: notes
25–30 min. Ask them to tick these live and put the count in the chat — instant picture of readiness.
:::

## Two honest reminders 💛 {.smaller}

**Small and working > big and broken** 🌱

If something is half-finished, say so in the README. Honesty is not a penalty.

. . .

**If you used AI**, that's allowed for explaining and debugging — but next week you explain the code yourself.
So go through it now, line by line. 📖

::: notes
30–40 min. Non-accusatory framing. The message is "protect yourself", not "I'm watching you".
:::

## Work time 🛠️ {.smaller}

⏱️ Rest of the block

- ✋ Raise your hand — I join your room
- 👥 Rooms open for pair debugging
- 💬 Chat for quick questions

**Practice tip:** explain your code out loud to your partner. If you can explain it, you're ready. 🗣️

::: notes
40–75 min. Rubber-duck explaining is the single best exam preparation.
:::

## Before you go 📌 {.smaller}

1. Push everything 💾
2. Sign up for an exam slot: [link] 📅
3. Check your tool runs on a **clean clone** of your repo:

```bash
git clone <your repo> test-clone
cd test-clone
python3 scripts/my_tool.py data/sequences.fasta
```

. . .

See you next week 💛

::: notes
75–80 min. The clean-clone test catches missing files — a very common exam-day surprise.
